options.content:
When the agent is working, and whether that is when people are

Every agent event stamped with its hour and weekday in the timezone you pick. The grid is the page: a normal working week is a warm block from nine to six, Monday to Friday. Warmth outside it is either people working late or agents left running — the page cannot tell which, and says so. Session depth by starting hour shows whether the long delegated tasks start at the end of the day.

panels.title: Agent activity by weekday and hour
panels.description: Events per hour of the week, as a grid: rows are days, columns are hours in the chosen timezone, colour is volume. The working week should be a warm block from nine to six; anything warm outside it is worth a question. Empty cells are hours with nothing, not zero events.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT CASE DAYOFWEEK(CONVERT_TZ(FROM_UNIXTIME(e.observed_at/1000000000), '+00:00', '$tz')) WHEN 1 THEN '7 Sun' WHEN 2 THEN '1 Mon' WHEN 3 THEN '2 Tue' WHEN 4 THEN '3 Wed' WHEN 5 THEN '4 Thu' WHEN 6 THEN '5 Fri' ELSE '6 Sat' END AS `Day`,
       LPAD(HOUR(CONVERT_TZ(FROM_UNIXTIME(e.observed_at/1000000000), '+00:00', '$tz')),2,'0') AS `Hour`, COUNT(*) AS `events`
FROM whodunit_events e WHERE e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()*1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo()*1000000000 AND e.agent IN ($agent) GROUP BY `Day`, `Hour` ORDER BY `Day`, `Hour`

panels.title: After hours
panels.description: Share of agent events before 09:00 or after 18:00 in the chosen timezone. Agent time, not necessarily a person's — a long delegated task runs on after the person has left.

targets.rawSql: SELECT ROUND(100*SUM(HOUR(CONVERT_TZ(FROM_UNIXTIME(e.observed_at/1000000000), '+00:00', '$tz')) < 9 OR HOUR(CONVERT_TZ(FROM_UNIXTIME(e.observed_at/1000000000), '+00:00', '$tz')) >= 18)/COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM whodunit_events e WHERE e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()*1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo()*1000000000 AND e.agent IN ($agent)

panels.title: Weekend
panels.description: Share of agent events on Saturday or Sunday in the chosen timezone. Same caveat: the agent was busy, which is not the same as a person being.

targets.rawSql: SELECT ROUND(100*SUM(DAYOFWEEK(CONVERT_TZ(FROM_UNIXTIME(e.observed_at/1000000000), '+00:00', '$tz')) IN (1,7))/COUNT(*),0) AS value FROM whodunit_events e WHERE e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()*1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo()*1000000000 AND e.agent IN ($agent)

panels.title: Peak hour
panels.description: The single busiest hour of the day for agent activity, in the chosen timezone, over the whole range.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT CONCAT(LPAD(t.h,2,'0'),':00') AS value FROM (
  SELECT HOUR(CONVERT_TZ(FROM_UNIXTIME(e.observed_at/1000000000), '+00:00', '$tz')) h, COUNT(*) n FROM whodunit_events e WHERE e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()*1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo()*1000000000 AND e.agent IN ($agent) GROUP BY h ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 1) t

panels.title: When sessions start, and how deep they go
Sessions by starting hour and depth
panels.description: Sessions bucketed by the hour they started, stacked by depth: chat under 10 tool calls, working 10 to 49, agentic 50 or more. Agentic sessions clustering late in the day is the hand-it-over-and-go-home pattern, and it is what makes the after-hours figure above mostly agent time.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT LPAD(HOUR(CONVERT_TZ(FROM_UNIXTIME(s.first_seen/1000000000),'+00:00','$tz')),2,'0') AS `hour`,
       SUM(s.tool_calls < 10) AS `Chat`, SUM(s.tool_calls BETWEEN 10 AND 49) AS `Working`, SUM(s.tool_calls >= 50) AS `Agentic`
FROM whodunit_sessions s WHERE s.first_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()*1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo()*1000000000 AND s.agent IN ($agent)
GROUP BY `hour` ORDER BY `hour`

panels.title: How long sessions run

targets.rawSql:
SELECT b AS `length`, COUNT(*) AS `sessions` FROM (
  SELECT CASE
    WHEN TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, FROM_UNIXTIME(first_seen/1000000000), FROM_UNIXTIME(last_seen/1000000000)) < 15 THEN '1. under 15m'
    WHEN TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, FROM_UNIXTIME(first_seen/1000000000), FROM_UNIXTIME(last_seen/1000000000)) < 60 THEN '2. 15-60m'
    WHEN TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, FROM_UNIXTIME(first_seen/1000000000), FROM_UNIXTIME(last_seen/1000000000)) < 240 THEN '3. 1-4h'
    ELSE '4. over 4h' END AS b
  FROM whodunit_sessions s
  WHERE s.last_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  AND s.agent IN ($agent)
) t GROUP BY b ORDER BY b

panels.description: Wall-clock first to last event. A session left open overnight inflates this — read it as span, not effort.

panels.title: Rhythm per person
panels.description: For each person: events, their busiest hour, and the share of their agent activity after hours and at weekends. Sorted by after-hours share. This describes when their agent was active, not their working hours; the two diverge exactly when work is delegated.

targets.rawSql:
WITH ev AS (
  SELECT e.contributor, HOUR(CONVERT_TZ(FROM_UNIXTIME(e.observed_at/1000000000), '+00:00', '$tz')) h, DAYOFWEEK(CONVERT_TZ(FROM_UNIXTIME(e.observed_at/1000000000), '+00:00', '$tz')) dow
  FROM whodunit_events e WHERE e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom()*1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo()*1000000000 AND e.agent IN ($agent) AND e.contributor IS NOT NULL),
peak AS (SELECT contributor, h FROM (
  SELECT contributor, h, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY contributor ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) rn FROM ev GROUP BY contributor, h) x WHERE rn = 1)
SELECT SUBSTRING_INDEX(ev.contributor,'@',1) AS `Person`, COUNT(*) AS `Events`,
       CONCAT(LPAD(MAX(peak.h),2,'0'),':00') AS `Peak hour`,
       ROUND(100*SUM(ev.h < 9 OR ev.h >= 18)/COUNT(*),0) AS `After hours %`,
       ROUND(100*SUM(ev.dow IN (1,7))/COUNT(*),0) AS `Weekend %`
FROM ev JOIN peak ON peak.contributor = ev.contributor
GROUP BY ev.contributor ORDER BY `After hours %` DESC LIMIT 25

panels.title: Agent activity by hour of day

targets.rawSql:
SELECT LPAD(HOUR(CONVERT_TZ(FROM_UNIXTIME(e.observed_at/1000000000), '+00:00', '$tz')),2,'0') AS `hour`,
       SUM(CASE WHEN e.agent='claude-code' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `claude-code`,
       SUM(CASE WHEN e.agent='codex' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `codex`,
       SUM(CASE WHEN e.agent='agy' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `agy`
FROM whodunit_events e
WHERE e.agent IN ($agent)
  AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
GROUP BY `hour` ORDER BY `hour`

panels.description: Stacked by agent. Hours with no bar are hours nobody worked — not missing data.

panels.title: Agent activity by day of week

targets.rawSql:
SELECT CASE DAYOFWEEK(CONVERT_TZ(FROM_UNIXTIME(e.observed_at/1000000000), '+00:00', '$tz'))
         WHEN 1 THEN 'Sun' WHEN 2 THEN 'Mon' WHEN 3 THEN 'Tue' WHEN 4 THEN 'Wed'
         WHEN 5 THEN 'Thu' WHEN 6 THEN 'Fri' ELSE 'Sat' END AS `day`,
       SUM(CASE WHEN e.agent='claude-code' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `claude-code`,
       SUM(CASE WHEN e.agent='codex' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `codex`,
       SUM(CASE WHEN e.agent='agy' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `agy`
FROM whodunit_events e
WHERE e.agent IN ($agent)
  AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
GROUP BY DAYOFWEEK(CONVERT_TZ(FROM_UNIXTIME(e.observed_at/1000000000), '+00:00', '$tz')), `day` ORDER BY DAYOFWEEK(CONVERT_TZ(FROM_UNIXTIME(e.observed_at/1000000000), '+00:00', '$tz'))

panels.description: Stacked by agent. A flat weekend is normal; a flat Monday may be worth asking about.

panels.title: Tools used, by agent

targets.rawSql:
-- Top 15 by total calls. Without the cap this drew every distinct tool —
-- 145 on the real lake — as one unreadable band of labels. MCP tools are
-- shortened to "server · tool" so the axis reads; the raw name is in the
-- MCP dashboards.
SELECT REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(e.tool, '^mcp__(codex_apps__|claude_ai_|plugin_[a-z]+_)?', ''), '__', ' · ') AS `tool`,
       SUM(CASE WHEN e.agent='claude-code' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `claude-code`,
       SUM(CASE WHEN e.agent='codex' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `codex`,
       SUM(CASE WHEN e.agent='agy' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS `agy`
FROM whodunit_events e
WHERE e.tool <> ''
  AND e.agent IN ($agent)
  AND e.observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
GROUP BY `tool`
ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
LIMIT 15

panels.description: Which agent reaches for which tool, from the tool calls recorded in each session — not a fixed list of features. Shows the 15 most-called tools; the long tail is on the MCP & Tools dashboard.

panels.title: Agent comparison

targets.rawSql:
SELECT a.agent AS `agent`,
       COALESCE(s.sessions, 0)      AS `sessions`,
       COALESCE(s.tool_calls, 0)    AS `tool calls`,
       COALESCE(e.events, 0)        AS `file edits`,
       COALESCE(e.`lines`, 0)         AS `lines written`,
       COALESCE(c.commits, 0)       AS `commits`
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT agent FROM whodunit_sessions WHERE agent <> ''
  UNION SELECT DISTINCT agent FROM whodunit_events WHERE agent <> ''
) a
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT agent, COUNT(*) sessions, SUM(tool_calls) tool_calls
  FROM whodunit_sessions
  WHERE last_seen BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  GROUP BY agent
) s ON s.agent = a.agent
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT agent, COUNT(*) events, SUM(lines_added + lines_removed) `lines`
  FROM whodunit_events
  WHERE observed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  GROUP BY agent
) e ON e.agent = a.agent
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT agent, COUNT(*) commits FROM whodunit_commits
  WHERE agent <> '' AND status = 'assisted'
    AND committed_at BETWEEN $__unixEpochFrom() * 1000000000 AND $__unixEpochTo() * 1000000000
  GROUP BY agent
) c ON c.agent = a.agent
ORDER BY `file edits` DESC, `sessions` DESC

panels.description: Every agent this machine has seen, whether or not it produced anything. An agent with sessions but no edits is running and contributing nothing measurable — worth knowing, and invisible in a merged total.

options.content: Read with care. After-hours activity is where the agent was busy, not where a person was; a task handed over at six and finished at eight is agent time, not overtime. The timezone applies to everyone, so a distributed team reads oddly until the events carry each person's own zone. Per-person rows show the 25 most after-hours people, not everyone.
